review_type: Independent algebraic and domain audit of the supplied candidate after reading the original texts; not independent discovery and not a new blind review

verdict.mathematics: The proposed specialized finite-weight-class certificate and both stated guarantees are correct under the explicit domain below.
verdict.graph_scope: A single application/input-class contribution from F and T to R is justified. It is not a whole proof of generic R, nor a claim that F/T imply generic R for arbitrary common scales. Use contribution.result/remaining and omit whole_result.
essential_presentation_repairs: PhiHat_e(empty)=B_e c_e(B_e) is generally nonzero. Do not claim that PhiHat literally satisfies the opening F_e(empty)=0 hypothesis of R. Invoke R's mandatory-background extension and its marginal-plus-envelope proof, and separately prove the envelope for baseline coefficient 1.

The beta maximum is over movable players/classes only. Fixed players have no nontrivial deviations and no weight-class requirement; arbitrary fixed-player scales must not be allowed to inflate or invalidate the asserted maximum.
State finite real eta>=0. Local minimum yields approximate PNE and strict-improvement descent; the quality comparison needs a global minimum. No polynomial-time global optimization guarantee follows.

exact_domain.game: Finite positive real player weights, finite resources, nonempty finite resource-subset menus, with empty strategies allowed; each resource delay c_e has nonnegative real coefficients and degree at most an integer d>=2. Individual cost is the sum of resource delays and does not include an extra factor of the player's own weight. Deviations recompute the true new load including the deviator.
exact_domain.fixed_players: Every absorbed player has exactly one legal strategy. Its strategy may be any resource subset including empty. B_e is the sum of these fixed weights using e and is independent of the state. A player with alternative strategies who merely does not move on a particular path is not covered by this absorption argument.
exact_domain.classes: At least one movable player. Let k>=1 be the actual number of global distinct movable weights a_1>...>a_k, with the same class labels on every resource. Fixed-player weights do not count toward k. If only an upper bound on k is supplied, construct the certificate at the actual number first; do not silently identify actual-class prefix weights with a different root normalization.
exact_domain.social_objective: W(s)=sum_e (B_e+X_e(s))c_e(B_e+X_e(s))=sum_all_players w_i C_i(s); OPT=min_s W(s). This is the full weighted social cost, not W_M=sum_e X_e c_e(B_e+X_e), and not the unweighted sum of individual costs.
exact_domain.parameter: For each finite real eta>=0, use Psi_eta=PhiHat+eta W on the original complete legal state space.

independent_derivation.claim: The triangular weights form a convex combination and provide a resource-independent common player scale.
independent_derivation.details: Let A=A_(d,k) in [1,d) solve A=sum_(j=0)^(k-1)((d-1)/A)^j. Put t=(d-1)/A, lambda_r=t^(r-1)/A, S_j=sum_(r<=j)lambda_r. Then lambda_r>0, sum_r lambda_r=1, S_1=1/A, S_k=1, and min_j S_j=1/A. T proves S_j w_i c_e(B_e+Y)<=Delta_i F_e^opt<=A S_j w_i c_e(B_e+Y) for a class-j movable insertion. The shift c_e(B_e+x) preserves nonnegative coefficients and degree. Thus h_i=w_i S_class(i) is common across all resources, including resources where some other classes are absent.

independent_derivation.claim: Every ordered potential in the mixture has an integral lower bound and a monotone right-endpoint upper bound.
independent_derivation.details: For any current movable-user ordering v_1,...,v_n, let u_0=0 and u_l=sum_(q<=l)v_q, X=u_n. Its potential is P_(r,e)=sum_l v_l c_e(B_e+u_l). Nondecreasing c_e gives integral_(B_e)^(B_e+X)c_e(z)dz<=P_(r,e)<=X c_e(B_e+X), including X=0. Convexity is available for the earlier triangular exchange argument but is not needed for this envelope step. Since the lambda_r form a convex combination, the same two bounds hold for F_e^opt=sum_r lambda_r P_(r,e).

independent_derivation.claim: The coefficient-1 fixed baseline gives the asserted stronger full-W envelope.
independent_derivation.details: Define PhiHat_e=F_e^opt+B_e c_e(B_e). Set L=B_e+X and G_e=L c_e(L). The lower chain is PhiHat_e>=B_e c_e(B_e)+integral_(B_e)^L c_e(z)dz>=integral_0^L c_e(z)dz>=L c_e(L)/(d+1). The middle inequality uses B_e c_e(B_e)>=integral_0^(B_e)c_e(z)dz. The last inequality holds term by term: integral_0^L a_p z^p dz=a_p L^(p+1)/(p+1)>=a_p L^(p+1)/(d+1). The upper chain is PhiHat_e<=B_e c_e(B_e)+X c_e(L)<=L c_e(L)=G_e. Summing over resources yields W/(d+1)<=PhiHat<=W. This proof includes pure-fixed resources, B_e=0, X=0, zero delays and W=0 without division. The baseline sum_e B_e c_e(B_e) is a state constant and changes neither local nor global minimizers for a fixed eta.

independent_derivation.claim: The full social marginal is valid in the original game with fixed background.
independent_derivation.details: For movable insertion weight w and new full load L=B_e+Y, the old full load is L-w>=0. For c(x)=x^p, G_e(new)-G_e(old)=L^(p+1)-(L-w)^(p+1)=w sum_(r=0)^p L^(p-r)(L-w)^r, so w c(L)<=Delta G_e<=(p+1)w c(L)<=(d+1)w c(L). Add nonnegative monomial coefficients, including p=0. This is the derivative-free form of R's full-W marginal and incorporates changes in the costs paid by fixed players. Adding the state-constant baseline leaves Delta F unchanged.

independent_derivation.claim: The claimed beta is a valid guarantee for every single-player local minimum and for strict-improvement descent.
independent_derivation.details: For a class-j movable player, Psi_eta has lower insertion scale w_i(S_j+eta) and upper insertion scale w_i(A S_j+eta(d+1)). Their ratio r_eta(S)=(A S+eta(d+1))/(S+eta) has derivative eta(A-(d+1))/(S+eta)^2<=0 since A<d<d+1. Thus max_j r_eta(S_j)=r_eta(1/A)=[1+eta(d+1)]/[1/A+eta]; eta=0 gives A for every class. For a true deviation split deleted, added and held resource costs as D,N,H>=0. The resource-state changes on held resources are zero. With h'_i=w_i(S_j+eta)>0, Delta Psi_eta<=h'_i(beta N-D)=h'_i[beta C_i(new)-C_i(old)-(beta-1)H]<=h'_i[beta C_i(new)-C_i(old)]. Therefore every strict beta improvement decreases Psi_eta, and any single-player local minimum is beta-PNE. Fixed players have no alternative strategy, so their constraints are tautological and they do not enter this maximum. If an all-player notation is desired for matching R's background subsection, choose fixed-player h_i/w_i=1/A; it adds no insertion obligations and no larger ratio.

independent_derivation.claim: Only a global minimum receives the asserted full-W quality guarantee.
independent_derivation.details: Let s_eta globally minimize Psi_eta and let o minimize W. The independently established m=1/(d+1), M=1 envelope gives [1/(d+1)+eta]W(s_eta)<=Psi_eta(s_eta)<=Psi_eta(o)<=[1+eta]W(o). Consequently W(s_eta)<=[(1+eta)/(1/(d+1)+eta)]OPT. The coefficient on the left is positive for all finite eta>=0. If OPT=0 the same chain gives W(s_eta)=0; no 0/0 ratio is used. A local minimum lacks the middle global comparison. Finite state space proves existence of these minimizers, not a polynomial algorithm to find a global one.

boundary_checks: k=1: A=1, lambda_1=S_1=1, beta_eta=(1+eta(d+1))/(1+eta); eta=0 recovers exact stability and the stated (d+1) global quality bound.
eta=0 for every k: beta=A and the quality coefficient is d+1. The envelope is a sufficient guarantee, not a claim of an attained worst-case ratio.
eta>0 finite: A<=beta_eta<d+1 and 1<=(1+eta)/(1/(d+1)+eta)<=d+1. The formal limit eta->infinity is explanatory only and is not an allowed finite input.
No movable players: the state is unique and exact, and W=OPT. Treat separately and do not define A_(d,0) or a minimum over an empty class set.
d=0 or d=1: separate exact-potential arguments are available in T, but the proposed d>=2 root formula is not asserted there.
Empty strategies, positive-cost moves to zero, zero-polynomial resources, ties and pure-fixed resources all remain within the direct inequalities. No cost division is needed.
Only global class labels are used. Resource-specific reindexing or replacing k by the maximum number of classes on a single resource would lose the common h_i certificate.
